the heterogeneity in the formation of mouse prion protein amyloid fibrils is modulated by salt in an ionic strength-dependent manner, and this modulation is because of the binding to the protein of anions that follow the electroselectivity order.

the pathway of mouse prion protein amyloid fibril aggregation can be changed by the addition of salt, that the pathway of aggregation can be changed from conformational conversion following fibril elongation to fibril formation following conformational conversion, and that this change in pathway occurs because of the linkage to anion binding.
NaCl modulates the pathway of amyloidd formation in the mouse prion by binding to the protein, and that this binding modulates the rate of amyloid fibrill formation by the protein.

the formation of amyloid fibrils from the prion protein, which are implicated in neurodegenerative disease.

how a change in aggregation condition, in this case the addition of NaCl, modulates the pathway of amyloidd fibril formation by a protein, as well as with how the heterogeneity in reaction conditions results in heterogeneity in fibril structure.

understanding the molecular mechanism of the formation of wormlike amyloid fibrils, which is important for the development of new therapeutic agents that prevent the formation of amyloid fibrils and for the development of a new generation of biomaterials that are more resistant to amyloid fibril attack.

NaCl modulates the pathway of amyloidosisis, which leads to heterogeneity of the amyloid fibrils.
NaCl at high concentration promotes fibril formation by binding to the protein, whereas at low concentration it promotes oligomer formation, which is then followed by fibril formation.
the effect of anion binding is to alter the pathway of amyloidoses, and that the pathway of amylosis is modulated by the nature of the salt.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
salt-induced changes in the pathway of worm-like fibrillar formation are because of changes in the binding and conformational properties of the protein.
the pathway for amyloid fibril growth is modulated by salt in a way that depends on the ionic concentration, the nature of the cation, and the nature of the protein.
the formation of the beta-rich oligomer is a rate-determining step in the formation of amyloid fibrils, and that this step is modulated by the binding of anions to the protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
salt can be used to modulate the heterogeneity inherent to the amyloid fibrillation process.
the formation of the amyloid fibrils of the prion protein is highly sensitive to the nature of the aggregation medium, and this sensitivity is not simply a function of the ionic strength.

the formation of wormlike amyloid fibrils is a complex process that involves the formation of beta-rich oligomers, which can have different structures, and that the kinetics of the reaction can be influenced by the binding of anions to the protein.
